name: Reef Eternal
geological_features: Planet-spanning coral reef structures breaking the ocean surface
Volcanic seamounts forming the reef foundations
Crystal-clear shallows averaging eight meters depth over the reef plateaus
Abyssal trenches between reef systems reaching twelve kilometers
specific_features: The Eternal Ring — a continuous reef formation encircling the planet at the equator
Reef structures that emit faint bioluminescence at night, visible from orbit
description: Reef Eternal is a medium oceanic world whose dominant feature is an interconnected reef system of staggering scale and biological complexity. The reefs break the surface in vast plateaus of white and pink calcified stone, creating a maze of shallow lagoons, tidal channels, and exposed flats that stretch for thousands of kilometers. Between the reef systems, the ocean plunges to abyssal depths where volcanic seamounts provide the mineral-rich foundations upon which the reefs have grown over millions of years.

The air above Reef Eternal is warm and salt-laden, carrying the sound of waves breaking endlessly against the reef margins. At night, the reefs glow with soft bioluminescence — blues, greens, and pale violets — transforming the planet's dark side into a constellation of living light visible from orbit. The water clarity in the shallows is extraordinary, allowing unobstructed views to the reef floor where schools of alien fish move in synchronized formations.

The Eternal Ring — the equatorial reef formation — appears to have grown along a precise geological line that suggests it follows an ancient tectonic boundary. The uniformity of its width and the regularity of its channel spacing have prompted speculation that the reef organism itself possesses a form of distributed intelligence, guiding its own growth with mathematical precision. Genetic analysis of the reef-building organisms reveals a single interconnected genome spanning the entire planet.

Pharmaceutical companies have identified over four hundred biologically active compounds within the reef ecosystem, several of which show promise in treating degenerative neurological conditions. Harvesting rights are fiercely contested, and the reef's apparent sensitivity to disruption has led to strict extraction quotas that are widely considered insufficient by conservation groups. The question of whether the reef constitutes a single sapient organism remains unresolved and politically charged.
